prior_narrative.tldr: DeepSeek said on Oct 20 it is open-sourcing DeepInfer, the software that serves its production models. Coverage first framed it as a way to cut AI operating costs, then as pressure on OpenAI and Anthropic.
prior_narrative.whats_new: No new DeepInfer coverage since Oct 21; Oct 22-26 items (agent evals, multi-agent and web-search papers) are unrelated and the efficiency claims remain unreproduced.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: A production-proven open inference stack gives platform teams a reference for serving cost and throughput that vLLM-style deployments can be benchmarked against.

status.detail: DeepInfer is public; independent reproduction of the efficiency claims has not appeared yet.

open_questions: Does an independent benchmark reproduce the 155T tokens/day and ~80% margin figures?
Which hardware backends does DeepInfer support outside DeepSeek's own clusters?
Which license terms govern commercial reuse of DeepInfer?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Read the DeepInfer repo and license before changing a serving stack; treat the margin figures as unverified until someone reproduces them on non-DeepSeek hardware.

prior_narrative.tldr: Reports on October 6–7 put DeepSeek's pre-IPO raise at $12B or more ahead of a 2027 listing. By October 11, Moonshot AI was reported to be negotiating a settlement with a shareholder before its own planned IPO.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Anthropic told investors quarterly revenue rose nearly 50% to $16.8bn ahead of its own IPO, putting a US lab alongside DeepSeek and Moonshot in the pre-listing queue.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Labs preparing to list will disclose revenue, pricing power and shareholder terms, which are the signals that tell you which vendors can fund inference capacity and price cuts through 2027.

status.detail: Three labs are lining up listings, but none has priced or filed publicly in these sources.

beats.headline: DeepSeek reported raising $12B+ before a 2027 listing
Moonshot seeks to settle a shareholder arbitration claim before its IPO
beats.summary: The claim reportedly seeks a 10.5% original stake and alleges misrepresentation.

beats.headline: Anthropic discloses $16.8bn quarterly revenue to investors

open_questions: Does DeepSeek's round close at the reported $12B or the later, higher figures?
Does Moonshot settle the shareholder dispute before its planned Hong Kong listing?
Does Anthropic publish an S-1 with pricing and compute-cost detail?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Keep a fallback provider for any lab whose IPO terms are unsettled, and re-check pricing commitments once S-1 style disclosures appear.

prior_narrative.tldr: Reinforcement Learning is a loose grouping of RL items, not one developing story. Since Oct 12 it has gathered a Qwen long-horizon agent report, an O-RAN benchmark, agentic-RL training papers, and AWS's SageMaker guide.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Oct 27: CoHARL co-trains agent policies with their executable harnesses, and EnvSched schedules environments under a fixed rollout budget; both are arXiv papers.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Agent RL is now judged on cost and reliability: EnvSched and calibrated budgets (Oct 20) target rollout spend, while MiRL and CalibraRL target named failures. All are paper-reported results, not production evidence; the SageMaker guide remains the only managed-platform recipe.

status.detail: A loose set of RL items; the newest aim at harness co-training, rollout cost, agent reliability and credit-assignment limits.

beats.headline: Alibaba Qwen introduces QwenGyre for elastic RL on extra-long-horizon agents
beats.summary: Reported via MarkTechPost; targets agent tasks that run far longer than standard RL rollouts.

beats.headline: X-RIC benchmarks agentic RAN controllers for reinforcement learning
beats.summary: Targets O-RAN controllers rather than LLM post-training.

beats.headline: Agentic RL papers: rollout budgets, stateful environments, search-state awareness, credit assignment
beats.summary: Four arXiv papers on cutting rollout cost, extending RL beyond tool-centric settings, teaching search agents to assess their own state, and crediting individual decisions within an episode.

beats.headline: AWS multi-turn RL guide, plus stability, simulation, robustness and token-credit papers
beats.summary: A managed-platform recipe on SageMaker AI and four arXiv papers on rounding alignment, token credit, dialogue user simulation and robust RL.

beats.headline: Reliability turn: calibrated rewards, credit-assignment limits, error-targeted agent fixes
beats.summary: Oct 26: three arXiv papers aim RL at hallucination, when fine-grained credit hurts, and terminal-agent misbehavior.

beats.headline: Harness co-training and environment scheduling: CoHARL and EnvSched
beats.summary: Oct 27: CoHARL optimizes the executable harness alongside the policy; EnvSched targets rollout generation and verification cost.

open_questions: Does calibrated rollout budgeting cut MCP-agent training cost on benchmarks beyond the paper's own?
Does Qwen publish QwenGyre weights, code, or benchmarks that show the elastic RL gain on long-horizon agent tasks?
Does the SageMaker MTRL recipe carry from Wordle to tool-using agent tasks, and at what training cost?
Does twin-world credit assignment improve agent training on benchmarks beyond the paper's own?
Do MiRL's error-targeted fixes hold on terminal-agent tasks outside the paper's own benchmark?
Does EnvSched's scheduling gain hold on agent-RL benchmarks beyond the paper's own, and with which environment mixes?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you train tool-using agents, measure rollout cost per environment (EnvSched, calibrated budgets), log recurring failure modes for error-targeted RL (MiRL), and A/B fine-grained credit against episode-level reward; treat paper results as unreplicated until rerun on your own evals.

storylines.label: Large Language
storylines.latest_title: Incentivizing Self-Learning in Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning

prior_narrative.tldr: This page groups items by the shared phrase "large language models", so most of it is a reading list, not one thread. Oct 16-27 items cover sycophancy, code-translation hallucinations, search agents, steering and continual learning.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Oct 29: Mistral Large 4 is released, with vLLM day-0 support (sparse MLA, speculative decoding, NIXL prefill/decode on Blackwell) and a Hugging Face launch post.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Mistral Large 4 is the one item here you can deploy: serving support landed the same day as the weights, so self-hosting is testable now. The papers remain a reading list.

beats.headline: Narrative-induced sycophancy evaluated in LLMs
Hallucinations in cross-language code translation, with mitigations
Search-state awareness for RAG agents, and LLM materials-data extraction
Spectral interventions, KG-to-text benchmarking and Bashkir adaptation
Long-horizon search evals, steering, vulnerability screening, sequential feedback and memory replay
Mistral Large 4 ships with day-0 vLLM and Hugging Face support
beats.summary: A concrete model release, preceded by an Oct 22 pricing comparison naming it.

open_questions: Do independent benchmarks confirm Mistral Large 4's quality against DeepSeek and Cohere models?
Does the "9x price gap" comparison hold against first-party Mistral API pricing?
Does Reva's real-time screening keep false positives low enough to gate agent-written code?
Does CAMR's replay selection reduce forgetting on models larger than those in its experiments?
Does CANS steering preserve general capability on models beyond those it was tested on?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you self-host, pull Mistral Large 4 on the vLLM day-0 build and rerun your own evals and latency tests before swapping it in. Treat the Oct 22 price comparison as unverified until you check provider pricing pages.
